subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Inductors: Storing Energy in Fields
description: A micro-lesson that makes Inductors: Storing Energy in Fields usable.

hook.text: An inductor resists sudden changes in current. It's electrical inertia.

buildup.text: A coil of wire builds a magnetic field when current flows through it.

discovery.text: Energy is stored in the magnetic field, not in charge like a capacitor.

twist.text: Cut the current suddenly and the field collapses, producing a voltage spike.

climax.text: Inductors pass DC freely but choke high-frequency AC. The opposite of capacitors.

punchline.text: Inductors hate change — they fight any shift in current.

quiz.question: How does an inductor store energy?
options: In an electric field between its plates
In a magnetic field created by current flowing through its coil
In chemical bonds within its core material
